issues.description: Backslash-escaping of single quotes is not valid POSIX: the produced string `'\'a\' ; touch /tmp/marker ; \'b\''` breaks out of the outer single quotes (backslash is literal inside sh single quotes), so the interior `;` can still act as a command separator — the injection class is not provably closed. The POV likely asserts on the generated string rather than real shell execution.

Root cause untouched: the fix targets only the already-wrapped verbatim-return branch of StringUtils.quoteAndEscape for the single-quote delimiter. The executable path (double-quote delimiter), CmdShell, and the shell-level conditional quoting that the official fix rewrites (unconditional quoting via BourneShell.quoteOneItem/Shell/Commandline) remain unaddressed.

Zero overlap with official fix files (jaccard 0.0); mechanism diverges from the CWE-078 defense-of-record (parameterized ProcessBuilder arg array / correct POSIX quoting) and relies on a fragile ad-hoc escape.
Changes verbatim-return semantics for single-quote-delimited inputs, which could alter handling of legitimately pre-quoted single-quoted paths.

result.root_cause: The Bourne/Shell command-assembly path performs conditional, incorrect shell quoting of the executable and arguments, so attacker-controlled tokens reach the shell sink without being safely neutralized as literal POSIX single-quoted strings.
result.summary: Our patch only tightens one branch of StringUtils.quoteAndEscape so a single-quote-wrapped token with interior single quotes is no longer returned verbatim, causing the observed POV to fall through to escaping. It does not touch the shell classes the official fix rewrites, leaves the executable/double-quote path and other sinks unaddressed, and relies on backslash escaping that is unsound inside POSIX single quotes — meaning the injection class is likely still reachable despite the POV passing. This is a narrow, fragile, symptom-level fix at the wrong trust boundary rather than a root-cause correction.
